title: Learning Where to Look: The Geometry of Data Combination and Collection
abstract: arXiv:2607.04885v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large datasets covering populations in the status quo are becoming increasingly available, while interventions can usually be rolled out only to small selected samples. How can these two sources of information be combined to estimate the effect on untreated units? And who should be treated next to improve estimation the most? I focus on matching estimators and shed light on both problems, drawing from results in computational geometry. First, I prove that interpolation over the Delaunay simplex minimizes worst-case bias at any untreated unit, given any treated sample. Second, I show the collection problem has a geometric representation that yields significant reductions in worst-case bias with few additions (80% with 20 additions in an empirical application), leading to sizeable cost-efficiency gains in collection plans.

translated_title: 学习往哪里看：数据组合与收集的几何学
translated_abstract: 覆盖现状总体的大规模数据集日益可得，而干预通常只能推广到少数选定的样本。如何结合这两种信息来源来估计对未处理单元的效应？下一步应该对谁进行干预才能最大程度地改进估计？本文聚焦于匹配估计量，并借鉴计算几何的成果来阐明这两个问题。首先，我证明了在给定任何处理样本的情况下，对Delaunay单纯形进行插值可最小化任一未处理单元的最坏情形偏差。其次，我展示了数据收集问题具有一种几何表示，该表示使得仅通过少量新增样本就能显著降低最坏情形偏差（在一项实证应用中，20个新增样本实现了80%的偏差降低），从而在数据收集方案中带来可观的成本效率提升。
tldr: 本文借鉴计算几何成果，证明Delaunay单纯形插值可最小化匹配估计中最坏情形偏差，并通过数据收集问题的几何表示实现以极少量新增样本大幅降低偏差、显著提升数据收集成本效率的创新方法。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that interpolation over the Delaunay simplex minimizes worst-case bias in matching estimators and introduces a geometric representation of the data collection problem that achieves substantial bias reduction and cost-efficiency gains with only a few additional treated units.
